text: The following question stood in the name of  Mr Gan Thiam Poh –  13  To ask	the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) how many cases of high-rise littering are reported in 2015; (b) what is the number of resultant injuries and deaths; and (c) whether the current measures to deter high-rise littering are satisfactory.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: High-rise littering is an anti-social act and offence that can pose a threat to public health and safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NEA has been working with the Town Councils and grassroots organisations to remind residents of the dangers of high-rise littering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Due to the nature of the offence, high-rise litterbugs are traditionally difficult to apprehend.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: When feedback on high-rise littering is received, outreach and education efforts to caution residents against high-rise littering will be conducted by my Ministry, the Town Councils and grassroots organisations, and in most cases the situation will improve after these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: However, in cases of persistent high-rise littering, NEA will deploy surveillance cameras once a suitable deployment site has been identified.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NEA has stepped up the deployment of these cameras over the years and has conducted close to 3,000 deployments since August 2012.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Offenders who were prosecuted in Court received fines ranging from $700 to $5,600.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NEA will continue to tackle high-rise littering by deploying surveillance cameras and secure the conviction of high-rise litterbugs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: While the effective conviction of high-rise litterbugs will serve as a deterrent to would-be offenders, I would like to urge every member of the public to play his part to cultivate social graciousness, good habits and a sense of shared responsibility for the cleanliness and safety of our neighbourhoods.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: For example, in very extreme cases, perhaps, confiscation of their flats.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I believe there are some cases, where the litterbugs have been really recalcitrant despite many, many fines already imposed on the persons.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Also, one of the issues is that high-rise litterbugs continue to offend on a daily basis, thinking they can get away with it.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Will the Ministry consider revealing the identity of litterbugs who may be caught on camera so that the grassroots or agencies can then follow up with these persons and to try and persuade the persons to not litter in the future?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I want to thank the Member for her suggestions as well as her questions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First of all, for high-rise litterbugs, the fine is not compounded.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They have to attend Court and the Court will decide on the fines to be imposed.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But certainly, this is something that we can follow up on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding the acquisition of a property, we need to carefully consider this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In most instances, in fact, since we started the implementation of surveillance cameras, as I have noted earlier, we have been able to effectively enforce on a significant number of litterbugs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Last year, for instance, more than 800 enforcement actions were taken and we hope that this will be a deterrence.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Before we even deploy surveillance cameras, we undertake education and outreach efforts, including house-to-house visits.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In most cases, the littering would stop or improve.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Therefore, implementing the surveillance cameras acts as a deterrence.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, for recalcitrant offenders, we also have to look at the facts of each case.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In cases where it may be due to mental issues, we work closely with the grassroots, as well as with the family members, to see what assistance can be rendered, as well as to implement measures to prevent this littering from happening, for instance, even installing wire mesh across the grills of the windows to prevent the littering offence.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We need to look at each case separately and be mindful that some of these may be due to specific issues.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The reason I ask is that there are many near-miss cases.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Residents show me their clothes that were burnt by cigarette butts.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But whenever I asked for action, NEA officers would merely set up ambush and then they would give me the update that they did not catch anyone.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, I have the impression that NEA does not have sufficient surveillance cameras and it takes a long time for them to deploy the cameras.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, just last year alone, there were more than 1,000 camera deployments.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to monitor the situation on the ground to see if we need to deploy more cameras.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But let me assure the Member that we will deploy a surveillance camera when it is assessed that there is a need to do so when our outreach and education efforts do not resolve the problem, notwithstanding the fact that resources are ultimately finite and, like everybody else, we do experience resource constraints.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But having said that, if there is a need and it is feasible to deploy the camera, we will do so.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We need the time to do a detailed site assessment to determine the feasibility of the installation of the camera, as well as to further study where is the best position or the vantage point to deploy the camera to increase the success rate of catching the high-rise littering act, whilst safeguarding the privacy of residents around.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: In Clementi, some of my residents have had cigarette butts going into the home where there are young children.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some have reported faeces being thrown from high-rise sources.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: First, of the camera deployments, what proportion of deployments has led to identifiable perpetrators being successfully convicted or warned?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Second, would the Ministry continue upgrading the camera technology so that there can be better night-vision image acquisition as well as higher resolution images?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Third, I also second Ms Tin Pei Ling's suggestion that offenders could be named and shamed, similar to how litterbugs were dealt with some years ago.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We agree with Members that high-rise littering is an anti-social act and it is something that we must not condone and will not tolerate as it poses a threat to public health and safety.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: At the end of the day, I think all of us need to play our part to cultivate social graciousness, good habits, as well as a sense of shared responsibility.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Deploying more and more cameras really is not sustainable and it is also not desirable.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But having said that, we take every high-rise littering feedback seriously and, where there is a need to deploy the camera, we will do so.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The reason is that, very often, when we put up a camera, it may actually deter the litterbug from littering if he is aware that there is a camera focused on him or the unit.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In some instances, it could also be because of intelligence or understanding of the ground, the camera could be focused at the wrong column of flat units, or on the wrong column and then we will have to redeploy it.
